name: PowerShell - Test-NetConnection Port Check
description: Windows PowerShell built-in for testing TCP connectivity to a specific port. Returns TcpTestSucceeded: True/False, the remote IP, and interface details. Available on all modern Windows hosts — no extra tools needed from a foothold.
notes: TnC (tnc) is the built-in alias. Output fields: ComputerName, RemoteAddress, RemotePort, InterfaceAlias, SourceAddress, TcpTestSucceeded. Outputs to PowerShell objects — pipe to Select-Object or Where-Object for filtering. For scanning a range of ports use the ps-port-scan-loop card instead. Requires PowerShell 3+ (Windows 8 / Server 2012 onwards).

recommended.note: Extend to a range scan with a PS one-liner using TcpClient.
nc -z is the Linux equivalent from Kali.

defense.prerequisites: Compromised Windows host with PowerShell available (all modern Windows). No elevated privileges required for outbound TCP tests.
defense.why_it_works: Test-NetConnection uses the Windows TCP/IP stack to attempt a full TCP three-way handshake on the specified port. TcpTestSucceeded reflects whether the handshake completed. As a built-in PowerShell cmdlet backed by the NetTCPIP module, it is trusted, signed, and generates no unusual file system artefacts.
defense.misconfiguration: Internal hosts with open ports not filtered by a host-based firewall. Windows hosts where PowerShell script block logging and module logging are not enabled.
defense.impact: Confirms reachable services on internal network hosts from a Windows foothold. Used to pivot after initial access — identify SMB, WinRM, RDP, and database ports on other hosts before launching attacks.
defense.detection: PowerShell script block logging (Event ID 4104) captures Test-NetConnection calls if module logging is enabled. Network: full TCP handshake (SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK) visible in PCAP; IPS rules on sequential port probes. Process: powershell.exe with arguments visible in Event 4688 (command-line auditing on).
defense.artifacts: Windows Security Event 4688 (powershell.exe with -Port argument if command-line auditing enabled). PowerShell operational log. Network: TCP SYN to target host/port.
defense.prevention: Enable PowerShell Constrained Language Mode. Enable script block logging (GPO: PowerShell → Turn on Script Block Logging). Network egress filtering to restrict which ports internal hosts can reach.
defense.evasion: tnc alias is shorter and may evade simple keyword-based detection. Single-port checks generate far less noise than a range scan. Test-NetConnection is a LOLBAS — same binary used for legitimate admin tasks.
